memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And on the lampstand there are to be four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms. One bud shall be under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair — six branches in all. The buds and branches shall all be of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold. Then make its seven lamps and set them up on it so that they light the space in front of it." - Exodus 25:34-37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the detail about branches, buds, and blossoms, God states the lampstand's actual purpose: its lamps were to light the space in front of it. All that beauty served a function. In the Holy Place, where no natural light reached, this lampstand kept the darkness away. It existed to shine.

That is a helpful reminder. God does not make beautiful things merely for display. The lampstand was gorgeous, but it was not decoration — it was there to illuminate. Its glory was in its usefulness. Likewise, whatever God has formed in us is meant to shine outward, not to be admired inwardly.

Jesus said it directly: "You are the light of the world... let your light shine before others" (Matt 5:14-16). We do not generate the light ourselves any more than the lampstand made its own flame; it simply held the oil and let the fire burn. Our task is to stay filled and stay in place, letting Christ's light shine through our ordinary lives. In a world with plenty of darkness, God has set you somewhere specific to give light. Shine where He has placed you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I letting God's light shine outward, or keeping my faith to myself?
Where has God specifically placed me to give light in a dark space?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not generate light on my own — I only carry Yours. Keep me filled with Your Spirit and let Christ's light shine through my ordinary life to those around me. Amen.
